subject.title: feat: raise (or remove) 3-minute no-output watchdog cap on CLI requests

question: Should ordinary inherited resumed CLI-backed user runs keep the 180-second guard, move to a longer bounded default, or gain explicit disable/tuning semantics?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves the inherited resume guard after the configured-timeout fix, while the requested default or disable behavior changes availability and compatibility tradeoffs for existing users.

options.title: Approve a bounded longer default
options.body: Raise the inherited resume ceiling through the existing watchdog defaults, keep the watchdog enabled, and require regression plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Add explicit disable semantics
options.body: Accept 0 or null style no-cap behavior only with schema, docs, and compatibility proof for existing configs.

options.title: Keep the 180-second inherited guard
options.body: Leave current behavior intact and document existing per-backend watchdog overrides for operators with known long silent CLI workloads.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded longer default
recommendation.body: Raise the inherited resume ceiling through the existing watchdog defaults, keep the watchdog enabled, and require regression plus upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current maintainer signal is the PR 90912 verification that preserved the inherited resume guard while accepting configured-timeout scaling.
